name: Confirm what we read (extraction review)
hostSurface: A full-screen step in a capture → confirm → next loop over Mail Day, and re-openable from any Unconfirmed row.
purpose: Make the machine's guess into the user's confirmed fact before anything reaches bills, the calendar or a reminder.
contents: The photo pinned; the classification; editable payee, amount, due date, account ending, kind — each showing what was read and each independently correctable; per-field confidence; the same 'Remind me' control the Date sheet uses; two explicit commits, 'Add to bills' and 'Just file it'; and the confirmation 'Added to your calendar. We'll remind you {lead} before.' — never the word 'Paid'.
states: extracted, low confidence (uncertain fields flagged; commit still available)
AI unavailable → same screen, blank fields, 'We couldn't read this one automatically'
duplicate suspected (same payee + amount + due date already on the list)
permission-denied (member can 'Just file it'; 'Add to bills' disabled with the reason)
no claimed home → routed to the Date sheet
entryPoints: Upload completion in the capture tray
Any Unconfirmed row on Mail Day
visualization: Photo BESIDE fields, not photo-then-fields — the user is proofreading, so source and extracted value must be visible together; highlight the region a tapped field came from where OCR gives boxes. Confidence is expressed per FIELD (a hollow mark on the uncertain one), never as a single percentage score.
uxNote: The doc's 'editable chips (Due Oct 12 · $142 · Clark PUD · Confirm)' is F10's clumsiest choice: a currency, a date and a payee each want a different keyboard and a different control, and a chip row hides which value the model was unsure about. Chips stay only as the collapsed Mail Day row summary. Done N times per stack, this is a screen, not a sheet.
